description:
Step 1 of fz-kdt.107's cure (cold review 2026-09-01, protoE.patch in
session scratchpad rev107/, ~8 lines, measured green). fz-kdt.104's
drop rule (stands_in_for, callsite_dispatch.rs:~183) judges domain
containment on SEMANTIC surfaces; at the {:cont,X} vs {:cont,X}|{:halt,X}
site the two arms differ only by their reducer's closure literal
(#66closure[] vs #68closure[]) at a position runtime_type_test_envelope
already erases to fun_top -- is_subtype says not-contained, so the exact
pair kdt.104 was built to kill SURVIVES, order-protected, and
probes/halt.fz returns {:done,3} under a legal arm order.

FIX: judge containment on the OBSERVABLE (runtime_type_test_envelope)
surfaces; keep the same-callee conjunct unchanged. Measured (protoE):
lib 1534/0, corpus stdout 0/579 moved, 1 canon file moves
(enum_predicate_search), arm-reversal crashers 2 -> 1, halt.fz correct
under ANY order (the narrow arm is dropped so no order can swallow
:halt).

RED-FIRST GATE: halt.fz as a drive_test fixture asserting {:halted,3}
under the arm-REVERSAL knob (red at base -- today green only by arrival
luck).

SOUNDNESS OBLIGATION BEFORE LANDING (the review's named open question,
the builder must ground it and the refuter must attack it): dropping on
envelope-containment routes a value carrying closure #68 into a body
specialized on #66 -- prove a callable position erased to fun_top is
ALWAYS invoked indirectly at the surviving body (evidence for:
probes/q3b.fz, three reducers through one shared dispatch, correct on
interp+native; evidence needed against: the CallableConstructionFact
grounding path and fz-kdt.111's grounded-closure machinery). If a
grounded-callable counterexample exists, the envelope judgement needs a
grounded-position carve-out.
title: P1: the dispatch drop rule is blocked by closure identity at a position no runtime test can see
